Data Sources

The Federal Workforce Data site is primarily sourced from OPM’s Enterprise Human Resources Integration (EHRI) system. Other OPM data sources, including USAJOBS, are included as well.

EHRI

EHRI is the federal government’s central source for federal civilian workforce data. Through the EHRI system, OPM collects employee and payroll data from federal agencies on a regular basis, creating a comprehensive picture of the federal workforce. EHRI data is used by OPM, federal agencies, and the public to enable analysis of federal workforce trends and to inform policy and operations.

Data release process

Each month, OPM releases the EHRI data submitted by agencies in the previous month.

Most recent data release

Data released on: October 7, 2026 | For agency data from: August 2026

Next expected data release

Data released on: November 4, 2026 | For agency data from: September 2026

OPM works closely with shared service providers and federal agencies to collect and validate workforce data, which is submitted within five business days after the end of the month. This process allows time to review submissions, resolve any data issues, and prepare the information for public release. While some files may arrive late, OPM publishes available data on schedule and includes any delayed submissions in future updates.

Timely data is essential for supporting workforce planning, public accountability, and informed decision-making. However, timeliness must be balanced with other key dimensions of data quality—such as completeness, consistency, and accuracy. To support transparency, OPM provides a Data Quality page where users can view the results of validation checks for each data release. This allows users to identify potential issues with specific data by agency. In addition, a Missing Files Report shows which providers have not yet submitted data for elements in a given time period, helping users understand where data may be incomplete. Moving forward, OPM will release data more frequently—typically every one to two months—on a publicized schedule, with any known data quality issues clearly disclosed to ensure users have access to the most current and actionable information available.

Employee coverage

Executive branch

EHRI covers all federal civilian employees of the Executive branch, except for the following:

  • U.S. Postal Service

  • Postal Rate Commission

  • Central Intelligence Agency

  • National Security Agency

  • Defense Intelligence Agency

  • National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency

  • Office of the Director of National Intelligence

  • White House Office

  • Official Residence of the Vice President

  • Office of the Vice President

  • Census Bureau temporary workers

  • Foreign service personnel at the Department of State

  • Tennessee Valley Authority

  • Federal Reserve - Board of Governors (the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau is included in EHRI as an agency subelement of the Federal Reserve)

  • Public Health Service Commissioned Officer Corps

  • Non-appropriated fund employees

  • Foreign nationals overseas

  • Executive Residence

  • President’s Intelligence Advisory Board

Legislative branch

EHRI generally does not include employees of the Legislative branch. However, the following organizations are included in EHRI:

  • Government Printing Office

  • Dwight D. Eisenhower Memorial Commission

  • Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission

  • Ronald Reagan Centennial Commission

  • Medicare Payment Advisory Commission

  • U.S. – China Economic and Security Review Commission

  • U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom

Judicial branch

EHRI generally does not include employees of the Judicial branch. However, the following organizations are included in EHRI:

  • U.S. Tax Court

EHRI datasets

Agencies send data to EHRI through the Status, Dynamics, Payroll, and Training data feeds. This data is structured into EHRI datasets that each serve a specific analytical purpose.

Note: Training data is not currently available through the Federal Workforce Data site


Status

A snapshot of the federal workforce each month. Status data files include all active employees (in either a pay or non-pay status) for each agency’s workforce as of the last day of each month.

Frequency: Collected Monthly

Common analysis questions:

  • How many federal employees are there?

  • What is the largest agency?

  • What is the average salary of federal employees?

  • How many IT specialists work in the federal government?

Dynamics

The personnel actions that have been processed for employees during the biweekly reporting period. Personnel actions include hiring, separations, promotions, awards, and others.

Frequency: Collected biweekly

Common analysis questions:

  • How many people were hired to the federal government last year?

  • How many federal employees retired?

  • How many federal employees were affected by reductions in force?

Payroll

Payroll records for the federal workforce, collected at the end of each pay period. Payroll records include information on the time reported by employees (e.g., leave, telework) as well as pay information.

Frequency: Collected biweekly

Common analysis questions:

  • How has the use of administrative leave changed over time?

  • How many federal employees are teleworking full-time?

Data collection process

The ultimate source of EHRI data is the core human resources (HR) systems used by federal agencies to manage their workforce. Agencies use core HR systems to store and process essential employee information, including job titles, salaries, work schedules, and personnel actions like hiring and separations.

The EHRI data collection process includes the following steps:

  • Agency core HR system: HR specialists use a core HR system to manage the workforce.

  • File preparation: Agencies collect data from their core HR system and structure it in the EHRI format.

  • File submission: Agencies send the data files by the 5th business day after the reporting period.

  • EHRI data ingestion: OPM receives data files and works through any data transmission or quality issues with agencies.

  • EHRI data processing: OPM processes the data and structures it for reporting and analysis.

  • Data access and use: EHRI data is made available through the Federal Workforce Data site, FOIA data requests, data sharing agreements with agencies, and internally to government.
